character: Former family ski area south of Syracuse with about 760 ft (232 m) of vertical that operated from 1953 until Intermountain Management bought and closed it in August 2021. It is not operating; its lifts and assets were sold off and reports describe the slopes as overgrown.

season.typicalText: Not applicable: closed since August 2021 (last season operated 2020-21).
season.notes: CLOSED — no 2026-27 operation announced (Yelp listing marked closed, updated June 2026). Timeline: bought in 2015 by the Greek Peak owners (the Meier family became sole owners of that group in 2019); sold Aug 2021 to Intermountain Management (owner of Song and Labrador) for a reported $750,000 and closed immediately, with lifts and assets sold off. The NY Attorney General sued in Oct 2022; in 2025 Justice Robert Antonacci II ruled the purchase-and-closure violated the Donnelly Act (antitrust), and later reports cite a sought $4M fine. In Aug 2025 Intermountain offered the ~100-acre ski area to Douglas Wheeler for $1.75M; his attorney said reopening would take months and at least $2M. Whether the sale closed is unknown.
